features.name: One-tap reorder from history
features.description: Any past order gets a Reorder button that loads its contents into the cart for editing before checkout.
features.hmw: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual basket without rebuilding it item by item?

features.name: Saved regulars list
features.description: The shopper builds a 'My Regulars' list once and adds the whole set, or any item from it, in a single tap each week.
features.hmw: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual basket without rebuilding it item by item?

features.name: Per-item substitution preferences
features.description: At add-to-cart the shopper sets a rule per item: accept a suggested substitute, choose from a shortlist, or never substitute.
features.hmw: How might we make an out-of-stock item a decision the shopper makes rather than one made for them?

features.name: Live substitution approval
features.description: When the picker hits an out-of-stock item the shopper gets a notification with the proposed swap to accept, reject, or remove before dispatch.
features.hmw: How might we make an out-of-stock item a decision the shopper makes rather than one made for them?

features.name: Suggested alternatives at checkout
features.description: Cart items that have gone out of stock show two or three ranked in-stock alternatives inline, so replacing one is a tap rather than a new search.
features.hmw: How might we make an out-of-stock item a decision the shopper makes rather than one made for them?

features.name: Half-day delivery slots
features.description: Checkout offers a morning or afternoon window (or narrower) instead of a whole-day 'Monday'.
features.hmw: How might we give shoppers enough confidence in delivery timing to plan their week around an order?

features.name: Proactive delay notifications
features.description: An automatic SMS or push goes out the moment an ETA slips, stating the new delivery date.
features.hmw: How might we give shoppers enough confidence in delivery timing to plan their week around an order?

features.name: Seasonal editorial homepage
features.description: A curated front page that refreshes regularly with what's in season, new producers, and editorial picks, replacing the static popularity grid.
features.hmw: How might we help a browsing shopper encounter the people and the seasonality behind the food the way a market does?

features.name: Producer profiles inline in browse
features.description: Every product links to a rich, shareable producer story surfaced inside the shopping flow instead of buried in the blog.
features.hmw: How might we help a browsing shopper encounter the people and the seasonality behind the food the way a market does?

features.name: Personal impact summary
features.description: A running plain-language tally in the account area: local producers supported, average food miles, produce saved from waste.
features.hmw: How might we make the impact of shopping this way something a person can feel without studying it?

features.name: Monthly impact recap
features.description: An after-the-fact monthly message — 'this month your orders supported 4 farms and saved the equivalent of 3 trees' — designed to be shared.
features.hmw: How might we make the impact of shopping this way something a person can feel without studying it?

design_directions.name: Two Taps to Done
design_directions.summary: Win by making the recurring shop frictionless. Lead with reorder, up-front substitution control, and reliable half-day slots so the weekly order collapses to reorder, adjust, confirm. Discovery and impact stay secondary.
design_directions.differentiator: The entire weekly order is a reorder-plus-confirm flow; substitution and slot decisions are moved to the moment of adding an item so checkout is near-empty.
hmws_addressed: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual basket without rebuilding it item by item?
How might we make an out-of-stock item a decision the shopper makes rather than one made for them?
How might we give shoppers enough confidence in delivery timing to plan their week around an order?
design_directions.tradeoff: Does little for the exploratory shopper or for mission storytelling; GreenBasket risks feeling like a utilitarian Ocado clone whose only pull is produce quality.

design_directions.name: The Digital Market
design_directions.summary: Bet that GreenBasket's edge is the market feeling. Rebuild the storefront as a curated, seasonal, editorial experience with shareable producer stories and provenance woven through browsing, making discovery and impact the reason to choose it.
design_directions.differentiator: A refreshed seasonal homepage and inline producer narratives replace the flat grid; where the food comes from is visible everywhere you shop, not filed in a blog.
hmws_addressed: How might we help a browsing shopper encounter the people and the seasonality behind the food the way a market does?
How might we make the impact of shopping this way something a person can feel without studying it?
How might we make an out-of-stock item a decision the shopper makes rather than one made for them?
design_directions.tradeoff: Leaves the reorder chore and delivery uncertainty — the loudest, churn-driving pains — largely unaddressed, betting that differentiation retains users better than raw efficiency.

design_directions.name: Set It and Trust It
design_directions.summary: Shift the work from the shopper to the system. A standing basket the system drafts each cycle, proactive substitution and delivery messaging, and impact delivered as a monthly recap, so the routine shop needs almost no active effort.
design_directions.differentiator: The default state is a system-proposed order the shopper edits or skips; nearly all interaction becomes review and exception-handling rather than assembling a cart.
hmws_addressed: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual basket without rebuilding it item by item?
How might we make an out-of-stock item a decision the shopper makes rather than one made for them?
How might we give shoppers enough confidence in delivery timing to plan their week around an order?
How might we make the impact of shopping this way something a person can feel without studying it?
design_directions.tradeoff: Demands real up-front trust in the system — the exact trust that silent substitutions destroyed — and fewer hands-on-cart moments means fewer chances for discovery and add-on purchases.
